lyrics:
[Intro: low guitar riff alone, like a bass, then stomping kick]

[Verse 1: muttered, close, riff and kick drum only]
Everybody in this town has got a mouth and half a story
Passing it from porch to porch like plates of someone's glory
I heard it at the gas pump, I heard it in the pew
By the time it got to me I didn't know that it was you

[Riff Chorus: distorted guitar plays the riff, crowd chants it]
Oh, oh-oh-oh oh, oh
Oh, oh-oh-oh oh, oh
And the windshield vipers go
Back and forth, back and forth

[Verse 2: louder, yelping, cymbals crash]
So I'm going to load the car up with a blanket and a thermos
Drive until the radio forgets the way to find us
Let them have the gossip, let them have the square
I'll be somewhere in the weather with the rain in my hair

[Riff Chorus: distorted guitar plays the riff, crowd chants it]
Oh, oh-oh-oh oh, oh
Oh, oh-oh-oh oh, oh
And the windshield vipers go
Back and forth, back and forth

[Guitar Solo: slide guitar, screaming and simple, over the riff]

[Verse 3: quiet again, almost spoken, riff and kick]
When I was five I thought the wipers were alive
Two thin snakes that kept the weather off the drive
Now I'm older and I know what things are called
But I liked it better when the world was strange and tall

[Final Riff Chorus: loudest, crowd chant, crashing drums]
Oh, oh-oh-oh oh, oh
Oh, oh-oh-oh oh, oh
And the windshield vipers go
Back and forth, back and forth
Oh, oh-oh-oh oh, oh
Oh, oh-oh-oh oh, oh

[Outro: riff alone again, rain, wipers, stop]
Back and forth
producerBrief:
TEMPO / KEY / FEEL: 124 BPM, 4/4, E minor. A stalking, stomping march. Menacing in the verses, explosive in the riff sections.

VOICE: Male, high, raw and nasal, with a blues yelp at the top. Verses are muttered close to the microphone, almost conspiratorial. Verse 2 is shouted. A crowd chants the riff on a wordless syllable, recorded to sound like a stadium.

INSTRUMENTS: One electric guitar run through an octave-down effect so it sounds like a bass, playing a slow riff of a few notes. The same guitar with heavy fuzz distortion for the riff sections, and with a slide for the solo. A drum kit played with deliberate simplicity: a kick on every beat, then crashing cymbals and a pounding floor tom. No bass guitar. Nothing else.

ARRANGEMENT MAP: 0:00 Intro, the riff alone, then the kick. 0:16 Verse 1. 0:47 Riff chorus 1, distortion and chant. 1:10 Verse 2, louder. 1:41 Riff chorus 2. 2:04 Slide guitar solo over the riff. 2:27 Verse 3, dropped back to riff and kick. 2:58 Final riff chorus, twice as long. 3:29 Outro, the low riff alone, rain and wipers, stopping at 3:42.

PRODUCTION & MIX: Early-2000s garage rock recorded to tape: raw, dry and loud, two instruments in a room, no polish and no overdubs beyond the chant.

SIGNATURE MOMENT: The riff alone in the first four seconds.

MODERN POINT OF VIEW: Verse 3 looks back at a five-year-old's version of the world and prefers it. The gossip of the original is updated only lightly, because it has not changed.

EMOTIONAL ARC: Irritation, defiance, escape, and a moment of wonder.
